You’re an intellectually curious, proactive finance professional who enjoys connecting the dots and turning complex information into clear, actionable insights. You combine strong analytical skills and attention to detail with excellent interpersonal skills, allowing you to build credibility and work effectively with stakeholders at all levels, including C-level executives.

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, or another analytical discipline.

• Strong financial modeling skills, including cash flow and three-statement financial modeling.

• Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and detail-oriented capabilities, with a high standard for integrity, accuracy, and precision.

• Strong interpersonal, listening, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build credibility and work effectively with senior stakeholders.

• Master’s degree in Business (MBA), Finance, or another analytical discipline.

• Experience using AI tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar tools to improve productivity and analysis.

We build with AI. We lead with judgment.

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work.

73a0a928107b27be.description: **About Skedler** Skedler is the reporting automation solution for Grafana OSS, Kibana, and Elasticsearch. Enterprises, MSPs, and SOC teams use us to turn monitoring, security, and infrastructure data into scheduled, audit-ready reports. Reporting was the first gap we found. It is not the only one. This role exists to find the next one, and it may have nothing to do with reporting. Learn more about us at www.skedler.com **Why this role exists** * Our engineers build. We are not short of capacity. We are short of the judgement a DevOps or SRE architect builds up from running observability stacks in production, the judgement that says which problem is worth engineering time. * This is not another engineering seat. We are looking for a founder mindset: someone who has already hit a gap, cared enough to build something for it on their own time or their own budget, and wants a platform to take the next one further than a side project ever goes. * You bring the problem and the conviction. We provide the platform to build it on. **What you will do** * Find the gaps open source observability leaves behind, the ones teams close with scripts, manual effort, or by living with the pain. The deliverable is a written gap inventory, five to eight candidates, each with what it costs, what teams tried instead, and who would pay to remove it * Own the roadmap for the gap we pick, validate it before we commit engineering time, and work with our engineers on design and architecture * Adjacent gaps count. If the sharpest one you have seen sits next to observability rather than inside it, bring it **What we provide** * We can provide the platform for your next build: * Engineering capacity, so your idea does not stay a weekend repo * Access to our customers, enterprises, MSPs, and SOC teams, to validate before you build * Distribution and go to market through the Skedler channel and partner network * Budget and a roadmap we agree up front, with ownership of what you build **Who we are looking for** **Experience: Minimum 5 years relevant** * You have built internal tooling because the open-source project would not do what you needed. This is the main filter * You have put an open-source project of your own on GitHub. Send the repo and the star count. This is super important to us, more than a job title. Forks, contributors, and real users count too * You have run Prometheus, Loki, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Elasticsearch, Kibana, or a comparable stack in production, at a size where you hit scaling limits and had to engineer around them * You have operated observability for more than one tenant, customer, or business unit * You have run this in a real deployment model: self-managed Kubernetes, on-prem, air-gapped, or a regulated environment where managed SaaS was not an option * You have owned or influenced the observability bill and can say where the money and the headcount actually went * You decided where engineering time went, not just executed someone else’s design * You have validated an idea before building it by talking to users rather than reasoning from first principles * Plus, not required: contributor or maintainer status in the open-source observability ecosystem or experience applying AI to the stack **Tools:** Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, AI-based observability, any open-source observability stack **Terms** Contract, converting to a full-time role on a roadmap we agree up front. Full-time hours, remote, work from anywhere. **To apply** Send your answers to hiring@guidanz.com. Answer all five. Questions 3, 4, and 5 are the ones we weigh most. 1. **What stack did you run, at what scale, and how was it deployed?** Numbers where you have them. 2. **Have you put together an open source project on GitHub, and how many stars does it have?** Link the repos you started or maintain, and tell us whether you still maintain them. 3. **What projects have you worked on, and what did you build in-house instead of using what already existed?** What happened to it afterwards, who maintained it, and is it still running? 4. **What gaps do you observe in open source observability?** Rank your top three, one line each. For the first, what did it cost in time, money, or headcount, how many other teams have you seen with the same gap, and what did you try instead? 5. **Why could you not solve this problem?** What stopped you on that first gap, time, access, budget, or team buy-in? What would you do differently with engineering capacity behind you? No length limit on questions 2 to 5. Link public evidence where it exists: repo, talk, blog post, or OSS contribution.

The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like.

Within a year you are successful if
• 
Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests
• 
The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time
• 
Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration
• 
Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported
• 
Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact
• 
Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced
• 
At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit

What you will be doing
Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day.
Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830.
Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures.
Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger.
Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes.
Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor.
Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start.
Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you.
Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants.
External providers. We produce revenue in-house, our Swiss accountants produce their piece, and our outsourced firm assembles the close. You will own the checklist, the policies, and the reconciliations, so providers execute against a Notabene-owned close rather than holding it themselves.

What you bring
• 
Experience as a Controller, Assistant Controller, or Senior Accounting Manager at a venture-backed company, with a track record of raising the standard on process rather than just running what exists
• 
You have taken a company through a first external audit and can describe specifically what broke and what you did about it
• 
Month-end close ownership across two or more legal entities in different currencies
• 
Deep, hands-on ASC 606, applied to at least one revenue model without clean precedent, and defended to an auditor
• 
You operate in the detail. You build the calendar, do the reconciliations, and touch the ledger
• 
Experience developing a small team or a single direct report

Nice to have
• 
Active CPA license
• 
Usage-based or consumption billing experience, particularly Tabs, Metronome, Maxio, or similar
• 
Public accounting background, especially audit
• 
Software development capitalization under ASC 350-40, including the time capture that makes it auditable
• 
Experience replacing manual accounting work with automation, and a clear view on what should stay manual
• 
Swiss entity experience, including CHF functional currency and Swiss statutory or VAT exposure
• 
Digital assets, payments, or regulated financial services exposure
